newsitem.title: UK: New bid throws Notts Forest takeover game wide open.
newsitem.headline: New bid throws Notts Forest takeover game wide open.

text.p: Two investment groups were fighting over English premiership stragglers Nottingham Forest on Monday in a move that could see the once-mighty soccer club get the cash it needs to sign top players and float on the stock market.

In a last-minute bid only hours before shareholders were due to vote on a 13-million-pound offer from a rival consortium, Nigel Wray, chairman of property group Burford, was set to offer a deal worth around 15 million pounds ($25.33 million).

"Wray is looking to inject between 10 and 12 million pounds plus loan stock and make sure shareholders retain a stake in the business...The offer is worth around 15 million and an eventual flotation cannot be ruled out," a spokesman for Wray said.

Notts Forest club officials said shareholders would convene for an extraordinary meeting at 1930 GMT on Monday to vote on the existing, lower offer from a consortium led by Sandy Anderson, chief executive of Porterbrook Leasing.

Media reports said shareholders had been expected to give the go-ahead to that deal but Wray's counter-offer for the club that flourished under Brian Clough in the late 1970s and 1980s may now have thrown the takeover game wide open.
The battle for Notts Forest comes in the middle of one of its darkest seasons.

Languishing just off the bottom of the premiership after winning only three of its 21 league games this season, the beleaguered club saw its manager Frank Clark resign in December and move in short order to First Division Manchester City.

England hero Stuart Pearce has taken over as caretaker player manager but, echoing Clark's frustration at not being able to splash out on new talent, has made clear he wants his formidable commitment backed up with a cash pile.
Investors now appear to be queueing up to give Pearce, a popular England defender nicknamed "Psycho", the clout he needs to get Forest back on track.
Wray, who owns a majority in London rugby club Saracens and has brought exceptional talent there, is leading a group including former Tottenham Hotspur chairman Irving Scholar.

Newspapers said Wray's line-up also includes Marjorie Scardino, who will take over as chief executive of publishing group Pearson Plc this week. Scardino was unavailable for immediate comment on Monday. ($1=.5921 Pound)
